proposal.utterance: What kind of BFO entity is the disposition to recognize authority?

entities.label: DispositionToRecognizeAuthority
entities.rationale: A disposition to recognize authority is internally grounded in its bearer (e.g., an agent or institution) — it is a tendency or capacity that the bearer possesses by virtue of its own constitution or social formation, not merely by virtue of external assignment. BFO_0000016 (Disposition) covers internally grounded realizable entities that are realized in processes when the right triggering conditions obtain. The disposition to recognize authority would be realized in an ActOfAcknowledgment process (already in the ontology). This is a class, not an individual, since we are asking about the kind of entity.

relations.rationale: DispositionToRecognizeAuthority is a subclass of BFO_0000016 (Disposition), as it is an internally grounded realizable entity inhering in an agent or institution.
When triggered, a disposition to recognize authority is realized in an ActOfAcknowledgment (already in the ontology as a Process subclass), connecting the realizable to its realization process.

open_questions: Should DispositionToRecognizeAuthority be further distinguished from CourtAuthority (a Role) and ActorWill (a Disposition already in the ontology)? ActorWill is already typed as BFO_0000016 — is the disposition to recognize authority a species of ActorWill, or a distinct disposition class?
Who or what is the bearer of this disposition — individual agents, legal officials, institutions, or all of the above? This affects whether we need sub-classes per bearer type.
Is this question asking for a BFO typing answer only (no graph addition needed), or should DispositionToRecognizeAuthority be committed as a new class?
proposal.rationale_summary: The disposition to recognize authority fits BFO_0000016 (Disposition) because dispositions are internally grounded realizable entities — they inhere in a bearer and are realized in processes when conditions are met. Recognizing authority is not externally conferred (which would make it a Role, BFO_0000023) nor is it a static measurable property (which would make it a Quality, BFO_0000019). It is a capacity or tendency, grounded in the bearer's constitution (e.g., an official's trained acceptance of a legal hierarchy), that is realized in acts of acknowledgment. The existing working ontology already contains ActOfAcknowledgment (Process) and ActorWill (Disposition), so DispositionToRecognizeAuthority could be a subclass of BFO_0000016 and may overlap with or specialize ActorWill. I propose minting working:DispositionToRecognizeAuthority as a new Disposition class, but flag for the user whether this should instead be treated as a specialization of the existing ActorWill class.
